scopes.sites:read: See the pages in their Stacktree account: each page's address and settings, whether it has been opened and by whom, and what readers commented. Request it when they ask what they have published, whether someone opened a page, or what feedback came back on it. Not needed to publish, or to check on a page published with no account: that page's claim_token reads whether it has been opened and whether comments are waiting.
scopes.sites:write: Publish pages into their Stacktree account, replace what is on a page at the same address, set a passcode, an expiry date and who a page is for, resolve readers' comments, and delete pages. Request it when they want a page kept, changed later from another conversation, or managed with their other pages. Not needed for a one-off page: POST /sites with no sign-in publishes a private link that lasts 24 hours, and its claim_token updates it.

apis.description: Publish a page to a private link that opens with no account, update it in place, see who opened it and what they commented, and get a webhook when it is opened (MCP Events, MCP 2026-07-28).

The same over REST: publish (POST /sites, JSON or a file), update, passcodes, named links, opens (GET /sites/{id}/activity), comments, and webhooks that call you when a page is first opened, a named link is opened or a comment arrives (POST /webhooks), so you can tell your User in any channel.

registration_methods.description: RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration. The standard path for MCP connectors (e.g. claude.ai). Register, then run the OAuth 2.1 + PKCE authorization-code flow.

Long-lived API key (stk_live_...) for server-side or CLI agents. Create one in the dashboard and send it as a bearer token. Accepted on every REST route AND on the MCP endpoint at https://api.stacktr.ee/mcp, so an agent with a key needs no browser and no OAuth flow to speak MCP.

OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628), for an agent that has a human to ask but no browser to drive. POST the device-code endpoint (no auth) for { device_code, user_code, verification_url_complete, interval }; print the URL for the human; poll the poll endpoint every "interval" seconds until it answers { status: "authorized", api_key }. The key is handed over exactly once and belongs to the human's account, on their plan. Codes live 10 minutes; rate limited per IP.
No registration. POST a file to the publish endpoint with no Authorization header to get a private, unguessable URL that lives 24 hours.

Pay to provision a persistent identity with no human in the loop. The payment is the credential. GET the endpoint for the rail menu (which agentic-commerce protocols are live); POST the payment to receive an stk_live_ API key once. The key carries free-tier limits (3 pages in total, each expiring after 7 days, no email gates; passcodes do work); POST /unlock buys past them. Accepted protocols: x402 (USDC), MPP, ACP (Stripe shared payment token), AP2.

No registration and no key: the wallet that PAID for a page (x402 pay-per-publish) is its update credential. POST {"wallet":"0x…"} to the challenge endpoint, personal_sign (EIP-191) the returned message with that wallet, then send "Authorization: Wallet challenge=…,sig=0x…" on PUT /sites/{id}. Challenges are single-use, 5-minute TTL. Scope: content updates to pages carrying that payer wallet (adopted pages while the wallet stays account-linked). EVM EOA wallets only.

No registration, no key, no wallet: the claim_token returned by an anonymous publish is that page's update credential while the page is unclaimed. Send "Authorization: Claim <claim_token>" on PUT /sites/{idOrSlug} with a JSON body {"html": "..."} (multipart with a "file" field also works). Works on every rail, including Solana x402 payers, who cannot use wallet_signature. Scope: replacing the content of that one page, nothing else. It stops working the moment the page is claimed (claiming rotates the token into the account), when the page expires, and for a blocked actor. Rate limited per IP and requires a direct client connection.
